core.title: Keep every plan artifact parseable
core.given: The repository has plan artifacts under the plan root, outside vendored or generated trees.
core.when: The plan tree is in scope for planning work or validation; this covers every such artifact, changed or unchanged.
core.then: Every in-scope plan artifact parses in the data format its file kind requires, including artifacts you did not change.
prefer: Fix the syntax the finding reports.
Treat parsing as the first gate: schema and identity checks only run once the artifact parses.
avoid: Leaving a plan artifact half-written or unparseable and relying on later rules to catch its other defects; they cannot see it.
Silencing the finding by renaming the artifact, moving it into a vendored or generated tree, or changing its file kind instead of fixing the syntax.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned: a path containing a directory segment this rule's check classifies as vendored or generated is out of scope; the exact segment names are this rule's own realization data, not a stack-wide list.
core.why: An artifact that does not parse is invisible to every other rule, so its defects hide behind one error.
evidence: The plan-integrity check parses every in-scope plan artifact and reports no parse finding.
A reviewer can load every in-scope plan artifact with the parser for its file kind without error.
verification: Scan scope: every plan artifact under the plan root whose file kind is a plan-artifact kind, changed or not. Exclusions: the check skips any path containing a directory segment it classifies as vendored or generated; that exact classification is owned by this rule's check and is deliberately not taken from the stack-wide excluded-list profile value; nothing else is excluded.
Each unparseable plan artifact yields one finding reporting the syntax error; per-rule severity 3, disposition strict: the rule fails on every finding, no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.
The check covers parseability only; schema and identity defects of an artifact that does parse are other rules' findings. Which parser a file kind uses is supplied by the realization.

fires: The repository contains any plan artifact under the plan root, whatever its plan-artifact kind, whether or not it was touched in the current change.
An unchanged plan artifact under the plan root is unparseable, even before any check has reported it.
The agent creates or edits a plan artifact under the plan root (example occasion).
The plan-integrity check reports a parse error for a plan artifact (example occasion).
doesNotFire: Files under a vendored or generated tree, i.e. a path containing a directory segment the rule's check excludes, even if they sit under the plan root.
Files under the plan root that are not of a plan-artifact file kind, for example free-form prose or notes.
Structured artifacts of those file kinds outside the plan root.

profileRequirements.meaning: Where plan artifacts live, so the core can scope 'the plan tree' and 'under the plan root' without naming a path.
Which file kinds (suffixes) count as plan artifacts and are therefore in scope and must parse; the format each kind denotes decides the parser.

bunOnly.text: Vendored and generated trees (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) are never scanned.
bunOnly.reason: The exact excluded directory segments are this rule's checker-owned classification in the Bun realization. The vocabulary's stack-wide excluded list is a union that also contains other trees, so this rule's exact four-segment set cannot be presented as that profile value; the core keeps only the conceptual 'vendored and generated trees are never scanned' and the exact names are carried here so instantiation skips precisely these segments.

bunOnly.text: The planner_plan_integrity validator parses every .yaml/.yml/.json under plan/ and reports no atdd-bun.planner.parse finding.
bunOnly.reason: Validator and finding ids of this rule are realization details; core verification and core evidence name the same check generically, and the concrete root and suffixes are profile values.

bunOnly.text: Scan scope: every file under plan/ with extension .yaml, .yml or .json, changed or not; skip any path containing a node_modules, dist, build or _generated directory segment.
bunOnly.reason: The plan root and plan-artifact suffixes are profile values (roots.plan, suffix.plan_artifact), but the exact skipped directory segments (node_modules, dist, build, _generated) are the rule's checker-owned Bun classification, not the stack-wide excluded-list profile value; they are carried here so the Bun instantiation skips precisely those segments.

bunOnly.text: Package rule: realized by a package guard (validator planner_plan_integrity) rather than a canonical planner node, but held to the same per-rule checks as every convention: a convention, strict, a failing fixture, relationship edges.
bunOnly.reason: This describes how the rule is realized and governed inside the ATDD-Bun package (package guard vs canonical planner node, validator ref, per-rule gate artifacts); it constrains the rule's own authoring, not the obligation on plan artifacts.

bunOnly.text: finding atdd-bun.planner.parse, reported by the planner_plan_integrity validator over the whole plan/ tree; a finding is one occasion to apply the rule, not a precondition.
bunOnly.reason: The finding and validator ids are realization details; the core keeps a generic parse-finding fact with the same observability, and the occasion-not-precondition semantics live in activation.fires.

neutralityNotes: The rule was already nearly neutral. 'Every .yaml/.yml/.json under plan/' became 'every plan artifact under the plan root of a plan-artifact file kind', with the root (roots.plan) and the file kinds and their formats (suffix.plan_artifact) supplied by the profile. The scan exclusions are handled as checker-owned: the exact vendored/generated directory segments (node_modules, dist, build, _generated in the reference) are this rule's own classification, carried in bunOnly on unless[0] and verifier_detail[0], because the vocabulary's roots.excluded is one stack-wide union (which also contains e.g. .git and repository-configured excludes) that this rule must neither redefine nor consume; core unless and core verification say the exact classification is rule-owned and that nothing else is excluded, so the Bun instantiation skips precisely those four segment names. Which concrete parser a file kind uses (the YAML or JSON parser in the reference) is left to the realization; the core only demands that the artifact parse. The validator/finding ids and the package-guard realization of this rule are bunOnly. Per-rule severity 3 and strict disposition are kept in core verification, not the profile. No proposed keys were needed.
